title: Your Real Hourly Wage Is Lower Than You Think
description:
A $60,000 salary for 40 hours a week works out to $28.85 an hour on paper. Add taxes, the commute, unpaid extra time and the cost of going to work, and the real figure in this example is about $18.15 an hour, over a third less. Work out your own number before comparing jobs or big purchases.

Example assumptions (yours will differ): 20% combined income and payroll tax, 4 hours a week commuting, 3 hours a week of unpaid extra work, $70 a week in work costs ($30 gas or transit, $30 lunches out, $10 clothes and other). Weeks averaged over the year.

#personalfinance #salary #careeradvice #moneytips #financialliteracy

scenes.say: You earn sixty thousand dollars a year. That's almost twenty-nine dollars an hour. Or is it?
First, taxes. In this example, about twenty percent goes to income and payroll tax. You keep forty-eight thousand.
Next, time. Add four hours a week of commuting, and three hours of unpaid extras, like early emails.
Then the cost of going to work. Gas, lunches out, work clothes. Say seventy dollars a week.
Put it together, and your real hourly wage is about eighteen dollars. Over a third less than it looked.
Why it matters: a three hundred dollar gadget doesn't cost ten hours of your life. It costs over sixteen.

scenes.say: And a job that pays a little less, but with no commute, might actually pay you more per hour.
